input.question: What caused the basement flooding—was it from a burst or leaking pipe in your own plumbing, or did the water come from outside (rain, groundwater, neighbor's property, etc.)?

input.value: burst supply line under upstairs bathroom sink

input.rationale: Water damage to the policyholder's own home (basement flooring, drywall, and contents) resulting from a burst supply line in the policyholder's own plumbing system is standard property damage coverage.

Extensive water damage across an entire basement affecting flooring, drywall, and contents typically exceeds $25,000 in repair and replacement costs, and requires prompt on-site inspection to assess structural damage, mold risk, and salvageable items.

input.claim_summary: Sam Patel's basement flooded due to a burst supply line under the upstairs bathroom sink, resulting in two inches of water damage to hardwood flooring, drywall (up to one foot), and stored boxes. Estimated damage likely exceeds $25,000; on-site inspection needed urgently to assess structural damage and mold risk.
